    StartersCoconut macaroonsChewy coconut and condensed milk mounds, baked goldenHow to make it250g desiccated coconut395g sweetened condensed milk1 tsp vanilla extract1 pinch salt2 egg whitesMix the coconut with the condensed milk, vanilla and salt.Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold through.Scoop 20 mounds onto lined trays.Bake at 160°C until golden on the edges.Cool on the tray.Christmas Eve cheese strawsPuff pastry twists with sharp cheddar, parmesan and cayenneHow to make it2 sheets of puff pastry80g sharp cheddar, grated30g parmesan, grated1 pinch cayenne pepperLay one sheet of the puff pastry on a tray, sprinkle with the cheddar, parmesan and cayenne, top with the second sheet and press.Cut into 2cm strips and twist each one.Bake at 200°C until crisp.House-blessing rosemary salt focacciaGeorge and Mary's bread, salt and grape juice for the Mocktail' new houseHow to make itAs written, serves 4Thick, airy focaccia dimpled with olive oil, rosemary and flaky salt, baked golden and served warm with good olive oil and balsamic for dipping.Mix 500g bread flour, 7g yeast, 10g salt and 400ml warm water into a wet dough.Cover and rest 2 hours, folding it over itself twice.Pour 4 tbsp olive oil into a 23 x 33cm tin, tip in the dough and stretch to the corners.Rest 45 minutes.Heat the oven to 220°C.Dimple deeply with oiled fingers, drizzle with more oil, scatter rosemary and flaky salt and bake 25 minutes.Serve warm with oil and balsamic.Devilled ham on saltinesZuzu's petals, and seconds for Uncle Billy.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsHoneymoon spit-roast chickenWhole chicken with garlic thyme butter, roasted over potatoesHow to make it1.8kg whole chicken50g butter, softened2 cloves of garlic1 tsp thyme leaves1 tsp salt1kg potatoesMix the butter with crushed garlic, thyme and salt and rub over the chicken.Cut the potatoes into chunks and set a rack over them in a roasting tin.Roast at 200°C, turning the potatoes halfway, until the juices run clear.Rest, then carve.Ma Bailey's pot roastSunday dinner at the Bailey house in Bedford FallsHow to make itAs written, serves 4Beef chuck browned and braised for hours with onions, carrots and potatoes in grape juice and stock until it falls apart, with thick gravy.Heat the oven to 160°C.Season 1.5kg beef chuck and brown well in oil in a casserole.Remove.Fry 2 onions in wedges for 5 minutes, add 2 tbsp tomato paste and 2 tbsp flour, then 200ml grape juice and 600ml beef stock, thyme and bay.Return the beef, cover and cook 2 hours.Add 4 carrots and 800g potatoes in chunks and cook 1 hour more.Simmer the liquid on the stove to thicken into gravy.SweetsGower's chocolate sundaeChocolate ice cream, hot fudge, whipped cream and a cherryHow to make it100g dark chocolate100ml thickened cream, for the fudge sauce1 L chocolate ice cream200ml thickened cream, whipped, for the topping4 maraschino cherriesMelt the chocolate with the cream into a hot fudge sauce.Scoop the ice cream into 4 tall glasses and pour over the fudge.Whip the cream, top each sundae and add a cherry. No coconut.DrinksEggnogChilled egg yolk, milk and cream custard drink with nutmeg, no alcoholHow to make it4 egg yolks80g caster sugar500ml milk250ml thickened cream1 tsp vanilla extract1 pinch ground nutmegWhisk the yolks with the sugar.Heat the milk and cream until steaming, whisk into the yolks and return to the pan.Stir over low heat until it coats a spoon.Add the vanilla and chill, which is the resting time.Serve with grated nutmeg.
